correctness.rationale: The product-chain resolvent gives the exact Laplace-transform ratio for target first passage, and renewal gives the exact mean with resetting. Uniform compact scaled-rate limits follow from exponential-polynomial domination. Explicit short-time bounds on numerator and denominator show normalized means diverge at both degenerate reset-rate scales. The limiting objective has one minimizer, proving both limits for every global minimizer. The zero-reset endpoint is finite and exponentially large in dimension, and the large-reset endpoint is coercive. Two independent finite computations checked 45 Laplace values and numerical optimizer trends; the infinite theorem is proved analytically.

value.rationale: A single corner in a growing binary configuration space is exponentially difficult to reach unaided, whereas resetting near the starting vertex can exploit short, direct fixed-length flip paths. The theorem determines a nontrivial polynomial exponent, sharp leading constant, and uniquely selected optimal rate scale among all Poisson rates. This is a motivated nonequilibrium search and transport optimization benchmark rather than a routine parameter substitution; it links rare-event geometry with resetting control.
